newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Nat.Grid front loads cost cuts.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Nat.Grid front loads cost cuts.

text.p: National Grid Group Plc, Britain's electricity transmission network, expects controllable cost cuts to be above 10 percent in the current year, averaging six percent over the next four years, finance director John Uttley said.
"We would expect the controllable cost reduction in the year we've just entered to be double digit, in other words greater than 10 percent," he told Reuters in a telephone interview.
National Grid has said it planned to cut its controllable cost base by six percent a year in real terms over the next four years to cope with a tough price review from industry regulator Offer.
The company agreed price changes with Offer which included a one-off, 20 percent cut in the current year last October.
Uttley also confirmed there would be job cuts of around 750 as part of the cost cutting moves.
National Grid saw pre-tax profits of 591.4 million stg in the year ending March 31, up 12.2 percent from pro forma results a year ago, and paid out a dividend of 11.13 pence per share.
Uttley said dividend growth was expected to be "four to five percent real for the next four years."
Overseas, Uttley said the company was "very happy" with returns from its operations in Argentina, with rates of return "in the teens," adding that National Grid felt it could improve that "a little."
National Grid is increasing its investment in Argentina by raising its stake in Citelec, which holds 65 percent of transmission business Transener, to 41.25 percent from 15 percent.
That will bring total investment there to 42 million stg, the company said.
National Grid will become the registered operator and Argentine industrial group Perez Companc will also own 41.25 percent.
Uttley said National Grid was looking at projects in India, Zambia and Australia as well as its interests in Argentina.
But he warned that, "it's a long haul overseas. They do not come quickly".
